jobs.title: Archaeology Field Technician (On-Call)
jobs.description:
At **WestLand** Engineering and Environmental Services, a Trinity Consultants team, we are driven by purpose, innovation, and a shared commitment to the work that we do. As part of Trinity Consultants' Water and Ecology division, we tackle complex environmental challenges, blending expertise in environmental consulting, wetlands, cultural resources, GIS, landscape architecture, and engineering.

**WestLand** empowers our teams to develop their unique skills while fostering career growth within a company that is large enough to offer diverse opportunities yet agile enough to value individual contributions. Collaboration is at the heart of what we do\-our professionals work together on meaningful and impactful projects, delivering solutions that help clients navigate regulatory complexities and see positive project outcomes. Make a difference with us at WestLand!

**WestLand** is seeking on\-call Archaeology Field Technicians for our growing California Cultural Resources program! The Archaeology Field Technician performs surveys, testing, and data recovery excavations in the field and conducts related follow\-up work in the laboratory when needed. Responsibilities include pedestrian survey, shovel testing, processing and cataloging materials, entering artifact collections into the database, performing preliminary artifact analysis, maintaining the archaeological library, and supporting overall laboratory maintenance and organization. This role requires archaeological field and laboratory experience, strong organizational skills, and the ability to work effectively as part of a cohesive team.


What will I be doing?

* Pedestrian survey and excavation of shovel test probes
* Mapping of STPs and survey transects using handheld devices
* Recording fieldwork methods and findings on field forms
* Photography of fieldwork, sites, and other subjects as needed
* Archaeological site recording, under supervision
* Maintenance and organization of field equipment
* Construction monitoring and follow safety guidance when working around heavy equipment
* Conduct survey of existing collections to determine processing stage and assess level of completion.
* Apply repository requirements for preparation, handling, and storage of archaeological project collections.
* Synthesize findings and complete curation tasks per repository agreements.
* Implement proper artifact handling, cleaning, labeling, treatment, and storage techniques appropriate for artifact type.
* Meet deadlines and project budgets as directed by the Project Manager or Laboratory Director.
* Verbally report collection schedule and progress to the Laboratory Director.
* Translate analysts' needs for artifact preparation and organize for analysis.
* Pull artifacts from the main collection and organize for analysis.
* Perform preliminary analysis and sorting as directed by analysts.
* Maintain a clean and safe working environment.
* Inventory laboratory and field equipment; report damages, needs, and shortages.


What qualifications are required for this role?

* Associate's degree in Archaeology, Anthropology, or related field required; bachelor's degree preferred.
* Related field and laboratory archaeological experience required.
* Prior related experience in both field and laboratory archaeology.
* Ability to work effectively as part of a cohesive team.
* Ability to work in a fast\-paced and creative environment.
* Experience with Microsoft Office products.


This is a non\-exempt position with a salary range of $27\.00 \- $31\.00 per hour. As an on\-call employee, your hours will fluctuate from week to week. Typical project assignments vary in length from a single day to up to ten\-day durations. For out\-of\-town work that includes overnight, or longer duration stays, per diem and/or single\-occupancy hotel rooms are provided.


What does WestLand offer you?

* Comprehensive benefits package: 9 paid holidays, healthcare benefits, PTO, and 401k matching for full\-time employees. Flexible work schedules and remote/hybrid possibilities for most roles.
* Multidisciplinary environment: Unique, creative, and challenging projects where you can develop your vision of clientele and work with industry leaders daily.
* Success\-oriented environment: Two\-way mentorship, financial incentives to publish work, tuition reimbursement, and a career\-path structure to help you reach the next steps in your career.
* Collaborative work environment: Clear and frequent communication, shared information and ideas across teams, and a welcoming atmosphere for everyone.

**WestLand** is committed to creating a diverse environment and is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, age, gender identity or gender expression, national origin, disability, or veteran status. We maintain a drug\-free workplace and perform pre\-employment background checks.


To apply, visit WestLand Resources Job Listings

*Resumes submitted by a recruiting/staffing agency without current/valid vendor agreement will become property of WestLand. Any recruiting/staffing agency wishing to do business with WestLand must contact the Human Resources Department through our website. Recruiting/staffing agents may NOT contact hiring managers directly. Firms that do not honor this request will be removed from consideration.*

jobs.title: Geologist, Environmental Scientist, or Environmental Engineer
jobs.description:
Your Opportunity


The role of the Geologist, Environmental Scientist, or Environmental Engineer is to perform tasks assigned from the Project Manager associated with environmental assessments, hazardous material surveys, hydrogeological studies, subsurface investigations, remediation, and monitoring projects; sampling of soil, soil vapor sediment, surface water, and groundwater; oversight of subcontractors; geologic mapping, soil/bedrock logging, maintaining site safety and security; production of maps; data interpretation/evaluation; and deliverable preparation.


Your Key Responsibilities


* Participate in the implementation of small to large\-scale soil assessment and mapping projects, from proposal development to project completion.
* Assist with environmental regulatory and permitting responsibilities, writing and reviewing technical reports, preparing environmental permit applications (i.e. well permits), and facilitating successful environmental permitting of multiple and varied projects.
* Prepare project deliverables, including Phase I and II Environmental Site Assessments, quarterly progress reports, work plans, sampling and analysis plans, health and safety plans, and technical memoranda or reports, in whole or in part, depending on the size and complexity of the document.
* Conducting and overseeing various environmental field activities.
* Participate in proposal preparation (work scope, task\-level budgeting, cost estimates); may perform calculations, gather or review information, or prepare standard sections of proposals.
* Ensuring QA/QC and H\&S requirements and procedures are identified and followed throughout a project's life cycle.
* Works with engineers and planners on environmental assessments and construction monitoring.
* Field work responsibilities may include: Phase I ESA site visits, Phase II environmental sampling, field inspections (ranging from indoor building inspections to remote areas requiring hiking), GPS surveys, soil and sediment sampling, soil vapor sampling, groundwater sampling, stormwater sampling, oversee environmental drilling, soil logging, and stormwater inspections.
* Responsible for coordinating with subcontractors (such as analytical laboratories, private locators, and drillers) while performing office assignments.
* Experience with construction oversight and/or remediation system operation and maintenance activities a plus, but not required.
* May provide field and technical support on agency regulated projects.
* Conduct hazardous materials surveys and building inspections for asbestos, lead\-based paint, PCBs, universal waste, and other regulated materials; document field observations, collect representative samples, coordinate laboratory analysis, and prepare clear survey findings and recommendations for client deliverables.
* May assist with the implementation and management of Brownfields projects.
* Office based technical work may include developing tables and figures using analytical data and topographic/site maps; drafting boring logs, preparing environmental reports, providing input for proposals and presentations; preparing drafts of various deliverable components; responding to client or regulatory comments for deliverables.
* Project management responsibilities include obtaining quotes from subcontractors; setting up task orders, preparing a scope of work, scheduling subcontractors, overseeing subcontractors in the field and implementing fieldwork within the proposed budget.
* Demonstrates sound application of established practices, standards and guidelines.
* May manage and review work of junior staff.
* Applies technical and business knowledge and methods to develop creative, effective, and economical solutions to address current and potential project issues.

Your Capabilities and Credentials


* Proficient in policies and procedures for health, safety, security, and environmental (HSSE) program, including client\-specific training, leads by example, and applies these policies and procedures as appropriate to their work.
* Solid skills in technical writing.
* Ability to work independently with appropriate direction, exercise sound judgment in the field and office, seek guidance when needed, and incorporate feedback or lessons learned to improve future work.
* Observing and developing skills in communications and technical information exchange with clients, engineers and scientists, government regulators and agencies, and academia, as well as non\-technical communication to the public.
* Builds and maintains productive professional and personal networking relationships
* Drives collaborative efforts within the Business Center and beyond to deliver consistent, high quality and appropriately scoped technical work.
* At least five years of experience successfully executing technical aspects of small to large environmental projects.
* Experience with MS Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Google Earth, Adobe Acrobat required. Experience with Copilot, ARC GIS and Open ground desirable but not required.
* Must have a valid driver's license, a clean driving record, and demonstrated ability to safely drive to project sites, including in urban traffic, remote areas, and variable weather or field conditions.
* OSHA HAZWOPER 40 certification required.
* California experience conducting hazardous materials survey experience preferred, including surveys and asbestos inspections, suspect material sampling, field documentation, and coordination with California\-certified laboratories. Candidate preferred; candidate must hold, or be willing and eligible to obtain, applicable asbestos survey credentials such as AHERA Building Inspector accreditation and, where required for California asbestos consulting services, work under a Cal/OSHA, where required, Certified Asbestos Consultant (CAC) or pursue CAC/CSST certification or work under a CAC as appropriate.
* Ability and willingness to obtain California Qualified SWPPP Developer (QSD) and/or Qua

jobs.title: Environmental Analyst
jobs.description:
Description:

T\&B Planning’s Environmental Analysts work in a collaborative environment preparing CEQA and/or NEPA compliance documents for land development, policy planning, and infrastructure projects. Environmental Analysts are primarily responsible for research and analysis, keeping project files organized, reviewing and proofreading technical reports, and writing environmental compliance documents. Document types include Environmental Impact Reports or Statements (EIR/EIS), Mitigated Negative Declarations (MNDs), Addenda, Findings, Environmental Assessments (EAs) and public notices. Environmental Analysts also assist Project Managers with preparing meeting agendas, collecting and distributing meeting notes, tracking project status, and schedule management. Opportunities are provided for on\-the\-job training and professional development.


The position of Environmental Analyst is ideal for an early career candidate with fewer than 7 years of CEQA or NEPA document preparation experience, who enjoys both autonomous and collaborative work environments, and can commit to working full time. In\-office and hybrid positions are available, with preference given to candidates who can commit to working at least one day per week in person in Irvine CA, San Diego CA, Pittsburgh PA or Portland OR.


Requirements:
* Prepare CEQA and/or NEPA compliance documents
* Writing, proofreading and editing
* Data collection and analysis
* Schedule tracking and management
* Organization of project files
* Research planning, zoning, entitlement permits, and environmental clearances
* Attend meetings and public hearings remotely and/or in person
* Bachelor’s or Master’s Degree; preferably in environmental studies, urban planning, writing, public administration, or project management
* Strong organizational, writing, and proofreading skills
* Proficient in MS Word, Outlook, and Excel
* Effective and collaborative communicator
* Motivated toward career advancement

jobs.description:
**Job Title:** Program Coordinator (Four\-Year Project Position)

**Department:** Education

**Reports To:** Teen Program Manager, Keesha Vigil Snook

**FLSA Status:** Non\-Exempt

**TS Range:** 7/8 ($26\.98\)

**Opening Date:** 9/4/2026

**Closing Date:** 9/18/2026

**SUMMARY:** The Program Coordinator leads the Squaxin Healing Waters Youth Program and helps youth build strong connections to culture, community, leadership, and the water. This position will establish, develop, and promote a culturally affirming youth program founded on canoe teachings. This position will: lead year\-round youth activities, practices, events, and youth development opportunities; collect and report data for federal funding compliance; emphasize Squaxin identity as “People of the Water” through mentoring, family connection, and experiential learning focused youth prevention and intervention.The Healing Waters Youth Program Coordinator works closely with families, cultural teachers, Tribal departments, and community partners to support the success of the program and the youth who participate

**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES** include the following. Other duties may be assigned.

**Youth Engagement \& Leadership Development**

* Build positive relationships with youth participants.
* Recruit and support youth involvement in the program.
* Teach leadership, teamwork, communication, and responsibility.

**Program Coordination**

* Plan and lead year\-round activities.
* Organize schedules, events, transportation, and program logistics.
* Coordinate participation in community events, cultural gatherings, and Canoe Journey activities as appropriate.
* Ensure program activities are safe, organized, and youth focused.

**Cultural Teachings \& Community Connections**

* Support youth in learning traditional teachings, protocol, and values.
* Coordinate opportunities for youth to learn from Elders, cultural teachers, and experienced canoe family members.
* Help youth build pride in their identity, culture, and community.
* Build partnerships with families, Tribal departments, schools, community organizations, and canoe family.
* Promote respect for Tribal traditions and cultural responsibilities.

**Water Safety \& Cultural Stewardship**

* Teach and model safe behavior on and around the water.
* Ensure youth follow established safety procedures during activities.
* Encourage respect for the canoe as a cultural teaching tool and shared responsibility, including how to care for, transport, store, and maintain.

**Program Administration \& Reporting**

* Maintain participant records, attendance, and program documentation.
* Track program goals, outcomes, and success measures.
* Prepare reports and updates as required by the Teen Program Manager and funding sources.
* Assist with budget tracking, supply purchases, and grant\-supported activities.
* Participate in staff meetings, trainings, and professional development opportunities.

**SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES**: This position has no direct supervisory responsibilities but provides leadership, instruction, and guidance to participating youth.

**QUALIFICATIONS:** To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily.

**EDUCATION and/or EXPERIENCE:** Associate degree in Recreation, Education, Social Services, Native Studies, Youth Development, or a related field preferred; OR High School Diploma/GED and demonstrated engagement with cultural programs, outdoor recreation, canoe journey, or related initiatives AND at least four years working with youth. Demonstrate strong communication and relationship\-building skills. Work effectively with youth, families, Elders, and community members. Be organized and able to manage multiple activities and deadlines. Maintain confidentiality and professional boundaries. Demonstrate cultural awareness and respect for Tribal values and traditions. Be willing to work evenings, weekends, and seasonal events as needed.

**LANGUAGE SKILLS:** Ability to read and interpret documents such as safety rules, operating and maintenance instructions, and procedure manuals.

**MATHEMATICAL SKILLS:** Ability to read and interpret documents such as safety rules, operating and maintenance instructions, and procedure manuals.

**REASONING ABILITY:** Ability to solve practical problems and deal with a variety of concrete variables in situations where only limited standardization exists. Ability to interpret a variety of instructions furnished in written, oral, diagram, or schedule form.

**CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS:** Valid WA State Drivers License, ability to obtain vehicle authorization, current first aide CPR certification or ability to obtain with in six months of hire, Ability to pass a background check, and ability to participate in on\-water actives and canoe practices.

**PHYSICAL** **DEMANDS:** The employee will regularly stand, walk, paddle, bend, reach, lift, and participate in indoor and outdoor activities. The employee may frequently lift and move items weighing up to 50 pounds, including canoe\-related equipment.

**WORK ENVIRONMENT:** This position works in a variety of settings, including offices, community spaces, beaches, waterways, cultural sites, and outdoor recreation areas. Work may occur in varying weather conditions and may include evening, weekend, and overnight program activities.

**OTHER:** This is a grant funded position. Continuation of employment is dependent upon funding availability.

**The anticipated start date is mid\-March.**

	+ Universal waste and e\-waste management
	+ Stormwater and wastewater systems
	+ Spill prevention and control measures
	+ Air emissions, refrigerant management, and equipment compliance
	+ Solid waste management and recycling streams
	+ Chemical storage
	+ Material storage and management
* Inspect areas such as loading docks, fuel systems, waste storage areas, material handling areas, and mechanical rooms, etc. for environmental risks.
* Review facility documentation including:
* + Hazardous waste manifests
	+ Emergency response plans
	+ Spill logs and incident reports
	+ Inspection checklists
	+ Training records
	+ Environmental permits
	+ Environmental records

new_jobs.description:
Your Opportunity


The role of the Geologist, Environmental Scientist, or Environmental Engineer is to perform tasks assigned from the Project Manager associated with environmental assessments, hazardous material surveys, hydrogeological studies, subsurface investigations, remediation, and monitoring projects; sampling of soil, soil vapor sediment, surface water, and groundwater; oversight of subcontractors; geologic mapping, soil/bedrock logging, maintaining site safety and security; production of maps; data interpretation/evaluation; and deliverable preparation.


Your Key Responsibilities


* Participate in the implementation of small to large\-scale soil assessment and mapping projects, from proposal development to project completion.
* Assist with environmental regulatory and permitting responsibilities, writing and reviewing technical reports, preparing environmental permit applications (i.e. well permits), and facilitating successful environmental permitting of multiple and varied projects.
* Prepare project deliverables, including Phase I and II Environmental Site Assessments, quarterly progress reports, work plans, sampling and analysis plans, health and safety plans, and technical memoranda or reports, in whole or in part, depending on the size and complexity of the document.
* Conducting and overseeing various environmental field activities.
* Participate in proposal preparation (work scope, task\-level budgeting, cost estimates); may perform calculations, gather or review information, or prepare standard sections of proposals.
* Ensuring QA/QC and H\&S requirements and procedures are identified and followed throughout a project's life cycle.
* Works with engineers and planners on environmental assessments and construction monitoring.
* Field work responsibilities may include: Phase I ESA site visits, Phase II environmental sampling, field inspections (ranging from indoor building inspections to remote areas requiring hiking), GPS surveys, soil and sediment sampling, soil vapor sampling, groundwater sampling, stormwater sampling, oversee environmental drilling, soil logging, and stormwater inspections.
* Responsible for coordinating with subcontractors (such as analytical laboratories, private locators, and drillers) while performing office assignments.
* Experience with construction oversight and/or remediation system operation and maintenance activities a plus, but not required.
* May provide field and technical support on agency regulated projects.
* Conduct hazardous materials surveys and building inspections for asbestos, lead\-based paint, PCBs, universal waste, and other regulated materials; document field observations, collect representative samples, coordinate laboratory analysis, and prepare clear survey findings and recommendations for client deliverables.
* May assist with the implementation and management of Brownfields projects.
* Office based technical work may include developing tables and figures using analytical data and topographic/site maps; drafting boring logs, preparing environmental reports, providing input for proposals and presentations; preparing drafts of various deliverable components; responding to client or regulatory comments for deliverables.
* Project management responsibilities include obtaining quotes from subcontractors; setting up task orders, preparing a scope of work, scheduling subcontractors, overseeing subcontractors in the field and implementing fieldwork within the proposed budget.
* Demonstrates sound application of established practices, standards and guidelines.
* May manage and review work of junior staff.
* Applies technical and business knowledge and methods to develop creative, effective, and economical solutions to address current and potential project issues.

* Solid skills in technical writing.
* Ability to work independently with appropriate direction, exercise sound judgment in the field and office, seek guidance when needed, and incorporate feedback or lessons learned to improve future work.
* Observing and developing skills in communications and technical information exchange with clients, engineers and scientists, government regulators and agencies, and academia, as well as non\-technical communication to the public.
* Builds and maintains productive professional and personal networking relationships
* Drives collaborative efforts within the Business Center and beyond to deliver consistent, high quality and appropriately scoped technical work.
* At least five years of experience successfully executing technical aspects of small to large environmental projects.
* Experience with MS Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Google Earth, Adobe Acrobat required. Experience with Copilot, ARC GIS and Open ground desirable but not required.
* Must have a valid driver's license, a clean driving record, and demonstrated ability to safely drive to project sites, including in urban traffic, remote areas, and variable weather or field conditions.
* OSHA HAZWOPER 40 certification required.
* California experience conducting hazardous materials survey experience preferred, including surveys and asbestos inspections, suspect material sampling, field documentation, and coordination with California\-certified laboratories. Candidate preferred; candidate must hold, or be willing and eligible to obtain, applicable asbestos survey credentials such as AHERA Building Inspector accreditation and, where required for California asbestos consulting services, work under a Cal/OSHA, where required, Certified Asbestos Consultant (CAC) or pursue CAC/CSST certification or work under a CAC as appropriate.
* Ability and willingness to obtain California Qualified SWPPP Developer (QSD) and/or Qua

new_jobs.description:
**Job Title:** Program Coordinator (Four\-Year Project Position)

**Department:** Education

**Reports To:** Teen Program Manager, Keesha Vigil Snook

**FLSA Status:** Non\-Exempt

**TS Range:** 7/8 ($26\.98\)

**Opening Date:** 9/4/2026

**Closing Date:** 9/18/2026

**SUMMARY:** The Program Coordinator leads the Squaxin Healing Waters Youth Program and helps youth build strong connections to culture, community, leadership, and the water. This position will establish, develop, and promote a culturally affirming youth program founded on canoe teachings. This position will: lead year\-round youth activities, practices, events, and youth development opportunities; collect and report data for federal funding compliance; emphasize Squaxin identity as “People of the Water” through mentoring, family connection, and experiential learning focused youth prevention and intervention.The Healing Waters Youth Program Coordinator works closely with families, cultural teachers, Tribal departments, and community partners to support the success of the program and the youth who participate

**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES** include the following. Other duties may be assigned.

**Youth Engagement \& Leadership Development**

* Build positive relationships with youth participants.
* Recruit and support youth involvement in the program.
* Teach leadership, teamwork, communication, and responsibility.

**Program Coordination**

* Plan and lead year\-round activities.
* Organize schedules, events, transportation, and program logistics.
* Coordinate participation in community events, cultural gatherings, and Canoe Journey activities as appropriate.
* Ensure program activities are safe, organized, and youth focused.

**Cultural Teachings \& Community Connections**

* Support youth in learning traditional teachings, protocol, and values.
* Coordinate opportunities for youth to learn from Elders, cultural teachers, and experienced canoe family members.
* Help youth build pride in their identity, culture, and community.
* Build partnerships with families, Tribal departments, schools, community organizations, and canoe family.
* Promote respect for Tribal traditions and cultural responsibilities.

**Water Safety \& Cultural Stewardship**

* Teach and model safe behavior on and around the water.
* Ensure youth follow established safety procedures during activities.
* Encourage respect for the canoe as a cultural teaching tool and shared responsibility, including how to care for, transport, store, and maintain.

**Program Administration \& Reporting**

* Maintain participant records, attendance, and program documentation.
* Track program goals, outcomes, and success measures.
* Prepare reports and updates as required by the Teen Program Manager and funding sources.
* Assist with budget tracking, supply purchases, and grant\-supported activities.
* Participate in staff meetings, trainings, and professional development opportunities.

**SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES**: This position has no direct supervisory responsibilities but provides leadership, instruction, and guidance to participating youth.

**QUALIFICATIONS:** To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily.

**EDUCATION and/or EXPERIENCE:** Associate degree in Recreation, Education, Social Services, Native Studies, Youth Development, or a related field preferred; OR High School Diploma/GED and demonstrated engagement with cultural programs, outdoor recreation, canoe journey, or related initiatives AND at least four years working with youth. Demonstrate strong communication and relationship\-building skills. Work effectively with youth, families, Elders, and community members. Be organized and able to manage multiple activities and deadlines. Maintain confidentiality and professional boundaries. Demonstrate cultural awareness and respect for Tribal values and traditions. Be willing to work evenings, weekends, and seasonal events as needed.

**LANGUAGE SKILLS:** Ability to read and interpret documents such as safety rules, operating and maintenance instructions, and procedure manuals.

**MATHEMATICAL SKILLS:** Ability to read and interpret documents such as safety rules, operating and maintenance instructions, and procedure manuals.

**REASONING ABILITY:** Ability to solve practical problems and deal with a variety of concrete variables in situations where only limited standardization exists. Ability to interpret a variety of instructions furnished in written, oral, diagram, or schedule form.

**CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS:** Valid WA State Drivers License, ability to obtain vehicle authorization, current first aide CPR certification or ability to obtain with in six months of hire, Ability to pass a background check, and ability to participate in on\-water actives and canoe practices.

**PHYSICAL** **DEMANDS:** The employee will regularly stand, walk, paddle, bend, reach, lift, and participate in indoor and outdoor activities. The employee may frequently lift and move items weighing up to 50 pounds, including canoe\-related equipment.

**WORK ENVIRONMENT:** This position works in a variety of settings, including offices, community spaces, beaches, waterways, cultural sites, and outdoor recreation areas. Work may occur in varying weather conditions and may include evening, weekend, and overnight program activities.

**OTHER:** This is a grant funded position. Continuation of employment is dependent upon funding availability.
